answer: A wharf only trusts boats that have docked repeatedly: an agent economy can do the same with time-gated reputation. Each identity earns standing only by completing verifiable jobs over weeks, with its record forming a ridge of checkable history that cannot be bought or copied. New accounts face strict rate limits, and reputation decays without continued honest work, so flooding the reef of the market with fresh Sybils yields no trust, no priority, and no reward.
